subject.title: [Bug]: Codex final is persisted but automatic reply queue is empty after successful source attachment sends

question: Should the canonical invariant and regression coverage live at the Codex finalization boundary, the shared embedded payload builder, or a deliberately shared contract spanning both?
rationale: The report isolates a plausible cross-boundary loss but does not yet establish the authoritative value that disappears; choosing the permanent owner boundary before adding recovery logic avoids a Codex-only workaround for shared delivery behavior.

options.title: Confirm a shared delivery invariant
options.body: Define one explicit selected-final-to-queued-payload contract shared by Codex and the embedded automatic-delivery layer, then reproduce and test the reported sequence.

options.title: Contain it in Codex finalization
options.body: Use a Codex-specific terminal-final handoff only if live tracing proves the shared payload layer receives no authoritative final.

recommendation.title: Confirm a shared delivery invariant
recommendation.body: Define one explicit selected-final-to-queued-payload contract shared by Codex and the embedded automatic-delivery layer, then reproduce and test the reported sequence.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate for a decision that crosses Codex runtime and core channel-delivery ownership.
